clue.text: He may be looked down on by the girl he woos

definitions.text: He may be looked down on by the girl he woos

parts.words: He may be looked down on by the girl he woos
parts.note: pictures a suitor singing up at a balcony while the woman he is courting gazes down at him

explanation.surface: A lowly suitor is scorned by the woman he is courting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looked down on' suggests contempt, but it is literal: the singer stands below her window or balcony and she looks down at him.
explanation.definitionFit: A lover who sings to his beloved beneath her window is performing a serenade, so she looks down at him.

clue.text: Plunders wines

definitions.meaning: to plunder a town is to pillage or loot it
sack was an old name for dry white wines such as sherry imported from Spain

explanation.definitionFit: Sacking a city means looting it, and sack is the old name for fortified Spanish white wine like sherry.

clue.text: Writer like Balzac, perceptibly on a roll

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Writer like Balzac, perceptibly on a roll': 'perceptibly' suggests a homophone, but no sound of 'on a roll' gives REALIST cleanly; the scan is blank and no search finds the printed clue.

clue.text: Quantity of thread required to secure borders of lace

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: something required is needful or necessary

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A seamstress works out how much thread she needs to sew lace edging in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' is a container signal; 'borders of' takes the first and last letters of 'lace'. Note that the definition is the whole phrase 'Quantity of thread'.
explanation.definitionFit: A needleful is the length of thread put through a needle's eye at one time for sewing.

clue.text: Book identifying old cat?

definitions.meaning: the fifth book of the Old Testament in the Bible
An elderly cat in T. S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats, so this name, placed after 'Old', identifies him

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second definition only works with 'Old' attached: the cat in T. S. Eliot's poems (and the musical Cats) is Old Deuteronomy.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the fifth book of the Pentateuch, and with 'Old' before it the name of Eliot's venerable cat.

clue.text: Legendary flyer takes up French horn

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking a word up means reading it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: cor is the French word for horn

explanation.surface: A mythical bird learns to play the French horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French horn' looks like the instrument but means the French word for 'horn', COR; 'takes up' turns it round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a gigantic mythical bird of Arabian legend, as in the tales of Sinbad.

clue.text: A prison officer's salary

definitions.meaning: British slang for a prison warder
old British slang for wages or pay

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link joining the two definitions, not a possessive: a warder is a 'screw' and so is pay, in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a jail warder is a screw, and a person's wages are also their screw.

clue.text: Starting at nursery level, one goes downhill fast

definitions.text: Starting at nursery level, one goes downhill fast

parts.words: Starting at nursery level, one goes downhill fast
parts.note: the nursery slopes are the gentle beginner runs at a ski resort, after which a sportsperson speeds down the mountain

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone whose life declines rapidly after childhood; the nursery is the beginners' ski slope and going downhill is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A person on skis learns on the beginners' nursery slopes and then descends the mountain at speed.

clue.text: Burden, having brother in control

indicators.note: the word for brother goes inside the word for control

parts.note: to rein something is to control or restrain it
Fra is the title given to an Italian friar, meaning brother

explanation.surface: Someone resents a burden of having their brother in charge of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burden' is used in its musical sense, the chorus of a song, not a load.
explanation.definitionFit: Burden is an old word for the chorus or repeated lines of a song, the same as a refrain.

clue.text: Dishevelled players showed distress

parts.note: the winds are the wind instrument players in an orchestra
someone who wept showed sorrow or distress

explanation.surface: Bedraggled musicians were upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair blown about by the weather looks windswept, untidy or dishevelled.

clue.text: Country house appears posh, after a couple of drinks

indicators.note: the word for posh comes after the two drinks

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea, one drink
tea is the second drink
U means upper-class or posh, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A country house looks rather grand once you have had a drink or two.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'couple of drinks' is two words for the same drink, CHA and TEA; 'appears' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French castle or large country house, often on a wine estate.

clue.text: Feature encompassing rejection of unsatisfactory dress material

indicators.note: one piece surrounds or encloses the other

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

indicators.note: a rejection turns a word back, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: food or a performance that is off is not up to standard

explanation.surface: A fashion item includes an unsatisfactory frock that has been sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejection of' turns OFF round to FFO, and 'encompassing' wraps the facial feature around it. 'dress material' is the definition, not 'dress' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiffon is a light, sheer fabric of silk or nylon used for dresses and scarves.

clue.text: It's not effervescing, for all that

definitions.meaning: describes water or a drink without bubbles, like flat mineral water

explanation.definitionFit: Water without bubbles is labelled this way, and the adverb also means nevertheless or even so.

clue.text: Outward features unknown in immortal saint

indicators.note: the unknown goes inside the word for immortal

parts.note: something immortal is eternal, everlasting
X is the classic algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An undying holy figure has an unknown outward appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Externals are the outside aspects or surface appearances of something, as opposed to its inner nature.

clue.text: Springer's been active? Then all is revealed

definitions.meaning: a springer spaniel flushes out birds, so game birds have risen into the air
the idiom said when a deception has been found out

explanation.walkthrough: A springer is a gundog breed that springs game birds from cover; 'Then' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase announces that a trick or scheme has been exposed, and literally means birds have been flushed up.

clue.text: Ben's neighbour? On the contrary

definitions.meaning: in Scotland a '... and ben' is a two-roomed cottage, the outer room beside the inner one
a conjunction introducing an opposing statement, like however

explanation.walkthrough: A 'but and ben' is a traditional Scottish two-room cottage: the but is the outer kitchen, the ben the inner room.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction introduces a contrast, and in a Scottish cottage it names the room next to the ben.

clue.text: Blooming radiation emission not involving uranium!

indicators.note: the letter for uranium is left out of the longer word

parts.note: fluorescence is light given off by a substance absorbing radiation
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A scientist notes a glowing emission that contains no uranium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' looks like an intensifier or a glow but is the definition, the botanical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Florescence is the process or period of flowering, so a plant in florescence is in bloom.

clue.text: Position of trainee serving time in minute, rebel leader's joint

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Position of trainee serving time in minute, rebel leader's joint': T in CADE'S HIP gives the answer, but 'minute' has no job in that parse (likely an OCR misread) and the scan is blank.

clue.text: Ounce of powder a son spilt crossing lake

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go across, round the letter for lake
spilt powder is scattered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A small amount of powder was knocked over by a boy walking past a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ounce' looks like a weight but is the big cat. 'spilt' rearranges POWDERASON; 'crossing' puts L into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ounce is another name for the snow leopard, the pale big cat of Central Asian mountains.

clue.text: Mostly work fast to get rich

indicators.note: most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: an opus is a musical or literary work
Lent is the Christian period of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Someone works hard and fasts to become wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the S from OPUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means wealthy or luxurious, displaying great riches.

clue.text: Part of theatre that's mine

definitions.meaning: the area in front of the stage, for the orchestra or the cheap seats

explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like a possessive but is the noun, a coal mine; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchestra pit or stalls area of a theatre, and also a colliery.

clue.text: Like serous membrane? More than one, it's said

indicators.note: the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: plural grammatically means more than one

explanation.surface: A biology student wonders whether there is more than one such membrane.
explanation.walkthrough: The pleura is the serous membrane round the lungs; the question mark admits the definition gives one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The pleura is a serous membrane lining the chest, and its adjective describes anything relating to it.

clue.text: Solicit loan from person getting work in pool?

parts.note: to touch someone is slang for asking them to lend you money
a type is a kind of person, as in 'not my type'

explanation.surface: Someone asks a fellow swimmer for a loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pool' suggests swimming, but it is the typing pool, the office room of typists; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Typists in an office typing pool would type by touch without looking at the keys.

clue.text: Dangerous description of Jacob's brother Esau

definitions.meaning: in Genesis Esau is described as a ... man, unlike his smooth brother Jacob

explanation.definitionFit: Informally a risky situation is hairy, and the Bible calls Esau a hairy man.

clue.text: Foreign character in British reserve force

parts.note: the reserve is always spoken of with its article, so the phrase supplies the definite article
TA stands for the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A foreigner has joined Britain's army reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign character' is a letter of a foreign alphabet, not a person. The Territorial Army, Britain's part-time reserve, is always 'the TA', so the phrase gives the article too; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, a character from a foreign script.

clue.text: Disheartened general leaves beauty for illicit liaison

indicators.note: the letters named depart from the word for beauty

parts.note: glamour is alluring beauty or charm

indicators.note: a word losing its heart keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A dejected army general abandons a beautiful woman for an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' reduces 'general' to GL, which 'leaves' takes out of GLAMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: An amour is a love affair, especially a secret or illicit one.

clue.text: List is examined at first by cohabiting couple

parts.note: a couple in a relationship are said to be an item
taken as written

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A living-together couple first examines a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to list things one by one, as on a bill.

clue.text: Native Australian depositing millions in some Western states

indicators.note: the letter for millions is put down inside the other piece

parts.note: the EU, the European Union, groups some Western European states
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: An Aboriginal Australian invests millions in Western countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native Australian' suggests a person, but it is the native bird; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless bird found only in Australia.

clue.text: Hard to get into revised score incorporating unknown movement

indicators.note: the letter for hard goes inside the rest
the rearranged letters take in the unknown
a revised text has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Z is one of the algebraic unknowns
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A composer finds it hard to get into a revised score that contains an unknown passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges SCORE; 'incorporating' adds Z and 'to get into' adds H, giving the musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a lively movement of a symphony or sonata, often the third.

clue.text: Bold fellow digesting Eliot, initially

indicators.note: taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a guy is a man or fellow
the poet T. S. Eliot's initials are T and S

explanation.surface: A man reads T. S. Eliot as his first step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' means the poet's initials, not the first letter of 'Eliot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutsy means courageous and determined, showing guts.

clue.text: Disliked having a French university in a London district

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: the university goes inside the district's name

parts.note: Poplar is a district of East London

explanation.surface: A French university in a London district is not popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link. POPLAR is an area in London's East End.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unpopular is disliked or not favoured by others.
